report.source_text: In histopathology, the tumor is composed of spindle to epithelioid cells exhibiting marked pleomorphism with vascular growth pattern. Strange nuclei, giant nuclei, and multiple nuclei can be seen in tumor cells. Interspersed mitotic figures and areas of focal myxoid change and fibrinoid necrosis showed features of high-grade sarcoma. The immunohistochemistry results of tumor cells were positive for EMA, vimentin, and CD68, focally weakly positive for CR, SMA, ckp and bcl-2, and negative for WT1 and GFAP.

report.source_text: Based on the diagnosis of pulmonary thromboembolism, the patient was transferred to the department of cardiovascular surgery for pulmonary thromboendarterectomy. Under general anesthesia (GA) and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), midline sternotomy was performed, and main pulmonary artery was opened. Grey white tissue mass in thrombosed areas was removed by separating it from the main pulmonary artery, bilateral pulmonary artery branches, and pulmonary valves. The diameter of the mass was 1.5 to 5 centimeter (cm), and the total length was about 20 cm.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old man presented with fever and dyspnea. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed elevated inflammatory markers (WBC 13400/mL, CRP 95.32 mg/L), elevated D-dimer (2.78 μg/mL), and elevated fibrin degradation products (FDP 20.81 μg/mL). Enhanced CT chest on admission demonstrated multiple filling defects in the main trunk of both pulmonary arteries and branches of the left pulmonary artery. Echocardiography revealed right heart strain with dilated right atrium and ventricle, impaired right ventricular systolic function, and abnormal echoes in the pulmonary artery. Color-Doppler ultrasound documented lower extremity venous thrombosis with blood flow stagnation. The clinical presentation mimicked acute pulmonary embolism, leading to transfer for pulmonary thromboendarterectomy. Under general anesthesia and cardiopulmonary bypass via midline sternotomy, a grey-white tissue mass (1.5-5 cm diameter, approximately 20 cm total length) was removed from the pulmonary arteries and branches. Pathological examination of the resected tissue confirmed high-grade sarcoma composed of spindle to epithelioid cells with marked pleomorphism, vascular growth pattern, mitotic figures, myxoid change, and fibrinoid necrosis. Immunohistochemistry was positive for EMA, vimentin, and CD68; focally weakly positive for CR, SMA, CKP, and bcl-2; and negative for WT1 and GFAP. Post-operative enhanced CT of head, chest, and abdomen revealed no other tumor tissue, indicating no metastatic disease.
